summary: promote() replays any prior promotion with the same attestation id without checking that it still describes current stable, and policy attestation ids are deterministic per (component, target, baseline), so a repeated identical rollback silently becomes a no-op reported as success.
failure_scenario: stable v1; promote v2 (evaluated); rollback() -> v1 (policy att id = f(rollback, v1, baseline v2)); promote v2 again via a fresh evaluated attestation; rollback() again mints the identical draft/id, promote() finds prior via promotion_for_attestation and returns the OLD record, so stable stays v2 while the caller is told the rollback succeeded.
evidence: Executed a credential-free repro against SqliteJournal with ComponentRegistry: after second rollback, stable==v1 is False and the returned record equals the first rollback's record (output 'after rb2 stable==v1? False same record True'). Cause: _policy_attestation_draft has no nonce/sequence, attestation_id_for hashes only the draft, and the replay branch at line 734-743 checks only component and to_version. plan_rollback_edge/plan_initial_promotion share the same draft so the durable command path is exposed too (not executed).

summary: promote() accepts a self-promotion (version == current stable, attestation baseline == version) and records a from==to history edge, after which rollback() no longer reaches the real prior version.
failure_scenario: stable history v1->v2; a journal-minted attestation with baseline=v2, version=v2 is accepted and stored as (v2,v2); rollback() reverse-scans history for to==v2, finds the (v2,v2) edge, picks previous=v2 and 'rolls back' to v2 (success, no pointer change); v1 is unreachable by rollback until another promotion.
evidence: Executed repro: self-promotion accepted (from_version==to_version True); subsequent rollback returned to_version==v2 and stable remained v2. promote_initial guards stable==version but promote() and promotion_attestation_faults have no version!=baseline guard.

summary: _load catches only ImportError, so an implementation module that raises any other exception on import crashes bind()/activate()/plan_registration with a raw exception instead of a named loadability refusal.
failure_scenario: A stored atomic version whose module raises RuntimeError (or SyntaxError) at import: activate() should return AdmissionError with 'not executable here (...)' faults, but the raw exception escapes and aborts activation of the whole manifest, bypassing itemized faults and any caller that maps AdmissionError.
evidence: Executed ComponentRegistry._load('badmod','f') against a module containing raise RuntimeError: it raised RuntimeError instead of returning (None, Loadability(...)). Pre-existing; tests in test_activation.py/test_registry_compat.py only cover missing module/qualname.

summary: Rollback is tested only once on a linear v1->v2 history, so neither repeated identical rollback nor self-promotion edges are exercised; both accepting-path defects above pass a green suite.
failure_scenario: The suite stays green while a second rollback of the same edge is a silent no-op.
evidence: grep of tests/runtime for rollback shows a single accepting-path test; no test re-promotes after rollback. (test_registry.py is outside the assigned list; noted for context.)

summary: InMemoryRegistryStore snapshot cut, CAS promotion and duplicate-definition refusal mirror documented contract on read; activate() checks resolution presence, loadability, implementation digest, capability revision, channel shape and endpoint. Whether executor_unavailability/leased/lifetime must also be enforced at activate() was not established (unverified).
Assigned test files under tests/runtime were not exhaustively audited line by line for guard reachability; only registry.py behaviour and rollback/activation coverage were reviewed in depth.
